newsitem.title: GERMANY: German chocolate makers may up prices this autumn.
newsitem.headline: German chocolate makers may up prices this autumn.

text.p: Cocoa futures rallies seen in past weeks could force Germany's chocolate industry to raise retail prices in the autumn of 1997, a statement from the confectionery association BDS said.
"If recent price developments are to become permanent, the industry won't be able to avoid price corrections in the autumn," it said.
BDS did not specify the amount of planned rises, nor any dates.
London cocoa on Tuesday was down a little after sell-offs last week, which had followed strong rallies in the second half of June.
But BDS said the mark's weakness and the high futures had combined to raise prices of German raw materials imports.

The relative strength of the pound and the dollar, which express international cocoa prices, had contributed to cost increases in cocoa beans by an overall 30 percent, or by 1,000 marks a tonne, since the start of 1997.
The industry's cocoa stocks were below those seen in recent years and this meant price increases were hitting processors directly and immediately.
Germany, which imports 300,000 tonnes of cocoa a year, was especially worried about potential crop reductions in the Ivory Coast, its main supplier, the statement also said.
